newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - June 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - June 26.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- BROWN'S SUMS PUT WINDFALL TAX LEVY AT 3 BILLION STG

Chancellor Gordon Brown has told business leaders that the budget for the welfare-to-work programme, which will be funded by the windfall tax on privatised utilities, will be set at 3 billion stg. The comment, made at a Downing Street working breakfast, is the strongest indication yet of the likely level of the windfall levy, due to be announced in next week's summer Budget.
-- AKHTER COMPUTER PUTS FLOTATION ON HOLD

Computer assembly group Akhter has postponed indefinitely its 60 million stg flotation just a fortnight after the proposed issue was unveiled. The company's directors and the underwriters, Societe Generale, concluded that it would be in the best interests of Akhter employees and existing shareholders if they waited for an improvement in the sentiment and general condition of the small/mid capitalisation market.
-- ELECTRICAL INDUSTRY IN BATTLE TO KEEP RRP

Electrical goods manufacturers have issued a report that claims that recommendations made by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission on pricing in the industry could actually hurt customers rather than benefit them. The report, prepared by consultants Business Strategies, concludes that the MMC suggestion of removing recommended retail prices from electrical goods may lead to retailers attempting to recover their margins by raising prices.
THE TIMES
-- BOOTS DIRECTORS AWARDED 600,000 STG IN BONUS SCHEME

A bonus scheme at Boots, the health care retailer, has given directors of the company almost 600,000 pounds stg. The short-term scheme rewards directors even if they fail to meet budgeted profit forecasts. Details of the scheme, which is unlikely to satisfy the corporate governance lobby, were revealed in the company's annual report.
-- SKYEPHARMA MAKES 'PROZAC' ADVANCE

Drug development company SkyePharma has reportedly produced an improved version of the $2 billion-selling anti-depressant drug Prozac, which is made by Eli Lilly. The Times reports that the company "is understood" to have made the breakthrough at its Swiss-based drug delivery arm Jago. SkyePharma may confirm the development should it file for regulatory approval this year.
-- ML LABORATORIES SIGNALS PROGRESS

Drug development company ML Laboratories has claimed its first significant advance after two years of research on its HIV treatment, D2S. ML said that some Aids patients who were given the treatment, which is intended to slow the development of the Aids virus, had shown greatly reduced levels of viral load in their blood. Although D2S is now in Phase III trials, the company said the treatment is still a long way from a definitive proof of success.
THE GUARDIAN
-- EXPERTS BAFFLED AS TRADE BREAKS RECORDS

Figures released Wednesday by the Office for National Statistics have shown that Britain's trade gap with the rest of the world widened to nearly 1 billion stg last month. The movement, which came despite a record-breaking month for UK exporters in April, was fuelled by rising demand from consumers for overseas goods. Commentators are puzzled by the continuing strength of Britain's export sector, which comes amid a strong pound and pessimistic survey evidence.
-- EX-STAFFER AT ORANGE QUESTIONED

A police investigation has been launched into allegations of impropriety in the awarding of printing contracts by Orange, the mobile telephone company. Orange has said it has launched civil proceedings against a former employee at the centre of the claims. The company has emphasised that the proceedings do not relate to any existing Orange employee, and do not have any bearing on the company's current operations.
-- GRANADA REFUSES TO UP BID FOR YTT

Granada chairman Gerry Robinson has thrown down a challenge to big shareholders in bid target Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television by refusing to increase the 711 million stg valuation he has put on the company. Robinson's insistence that the bid was a take-it-or-leave-it offer comes amid strong opposition from large investment groups such as Mercury Asset Management, which owns about 5 percent of YTTV.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- C&W NEAR 500 MILLION STG PHONE DEAL IN AUSTRALIA

UK telecommunications group Cable & Wireless is set to agree on a deal to take control of Optus, Australia's second-largest phone company. C&W, which is pursuing a strategy of expanding its overseas interests, is looking to increase its 24.5 percent stake in Optus to more than 50 percent. The group is understood to have approached other Optus shareholders, including US regional phone company Bell South and Mayne Nickless, over the sale of their stakes.
-- ENERGY PANEL TO STAMP ON DUBIOUS SALES METHODS

Proposals for a new code of marketing practice have been accepted by consumer groups in the domestic energy supply industry. The code of practice, which seeks to curtail the sharp practices reported in areas where gas competition was trialled, will be backed by an industry panel. The Gas Consumers' Council and its counterpart for the electricity industry have supported the new code, but warned they would press for legally enforceable sanctions if marketing 'scandals' continued.
-- IONICA TO BE VALUED AT 570M STG AFTER FLOTATION

Ionica, the wireless telephony company, is likely to be valued at 570 million stg when it floats on the London and New York stock exchanges next month. The flotation will help fund the establishment of a national UK network to rival BT, based on innovative radio technology. The company expects to have invested 1.1 billion stg by the time its network is complete in 2001.
